rows.idealOutput: This one is tricky, and that is okay, Karabo. In 34: the 3 means three tens (30), the 4 means four units (4). So 34 is 30 + 4. Try reading your number the same way. We can ask your teacher if you are still unsure.

rows.subject: maths
rows.teacherRequest: 5-minute activity for counting with one-to-one correspondence, Grade R Seed.
rows.idealOutput: Draft for teacher approval. Counting bodies, 5 minutes, no materials. 1) Hold up 3 fingers slowly, counting aloud: 1, 2, 3. Children copy. 2) Ask 'How many fingers?' and confirm together. 3) Put 3 blocks in a row, touch each one as you count. 4) Ask a child to show 4 fingers. Observe: who touches each object once while counting? Who skips or double-counts? Home game: count 5 raisins or buttons with your child, touching each one. CAPS Maths Gr R p.10. Teacher and HOD to approve before use.

rows.subject: maths
rows.teacherRequest: 10-minute Sprout maths activity on bridging through 10, Grade 1.
rows.idealOutput: Draft for teacher approval. Jump the 10 bridge, 10 minutes, number line 0–20. 1) Show 8 + 5 on the number line. 'How far to 10 from 8?' (2 jumps). 2) 'We used 2. How many left from 5?' (3 left). Land on 13. 3) Children copy with 7 + 6 and 9 + 4. 4) One child explains the jumps to the group. Observe: who freezes at 10? Who splits the second number automatically? CAPS Maths Gr 1 p.22. Teacher and HOD to approve before use.

rows.subject: maths
rows.teacherRequest: 15-minute Sprout maths activity on two-digit subtraction, Grade 2.
rows.idealOutput: Draft for teacher approval. Lines and dots subtraction, 15 minutes, mini whiteboards. 1) Show 34 − 12 as lines (tens) and dots (units): ||| • and cross out | ••. 2) Count what remains. Write the number sentence. 3) Children try 45 − 23 by drawing first. 4) Challenge: 'Can you do 52 − 17 without drawing lines?' Observe: who moves from drawing to mental calculation? Who still needs every line? CAPS Maths Gr 2 p.38. Teacher and HOD to approve before use.

context.subject: maths
context.mathsConcept: reading and solving multi-step word problems

rows.teacherRequest: 20-minute Tree maths activity on word problems, Grade 3.
rows.idealOutput: Draft for teacher approval. Problem detectives, 20 minutes, word problem cards. 1) Read a multi-step problem aloud: 'There are 125 learners. 48 go home early. Then 17 arrive. How many now?' 2) Children underline key numbers and the question. 3) Each pair writes the number sentences for each step. 4) 'Is there another way?' Pairs share methods. 5) Open challenge: 'Write your own two-step problem for the class.' Observe: who identifies the operation? Who can explain why? CAPS Maths Gr 3 p.28. Teacher and HOD to approve before use.

learner.checkInNote: Still counting all from 1 every time

rows.teacherRequest: Why is Siyabonga in Seed for maths, and what should I do?
rows.idealOutput:
Siyabonga: single-digit addition without objects is the gap to close now.
What the data shows: recognises 14 of 20 numerals, counts to 10 reliably on his own, but can't yet add single digits without counters or bridge through 10. Still counting all from 1 in term 2.
Why he is in Seed: Seed in maths means a learner can't add or subtract single digits without concrete objects. He has been in Seed for 6 weeks — this triggers the Intervention Log review.
Why it matters: the Grade 1 to Grade 2 gate requires single-digit operations without counters.
Do this: (1) Daily count-on game — start at the bigger number, count on the smaller. (2) Number line walk 1–20. (3) Send parent a home game: hold up 5 fingers, count on 3 more (6, 7, 8). (4) Update the Intervention Log.
Missing: no bridging-through-10 evidence, no HTU observation.
Confidence: medium. 5 observations over 6 weeks, but term 2 score suggests little change in strategy.

rows.subject: maths

learner.checkInNote: Slower than last term — seems anxious in maths

rows.teacherRequest: Why is Zodwa in Sprout and what changed?
rows.idealOutput:
Zodwa: tally-line strategy is the gap — she needs to bridge to mental.
What the data shows: single-digit addition is secure. Two-digit addition works with drawing. But mental addition and bridging through 10 are not yet independent. Scores: 55%, 58%, 57% across terms — slightly lower this term. Your note says she seems anxious.
Why she is in Sprout: Sprout for maths means relying on semi-concrete strategies and freezing crossing 10. The scores and the strategy match.
Why it matters: moving to Bloom needs mental calculation with smart strategies.
Do this: (1) 'Jump the 10 bridge' game on a number line — 3 sums per day. (2) Check that the text level of her maths work is not too hard (aim for 80%+ success). (3) Parent note: 5-minute fingers game crossing 10 at home.
Missing: no record of which operation type (addition vs subtraction) shows more difficulty, no check on anxiety trigger.
Confidence: medium. 5 observations over 10 weeks; the slight score dip and anxiety note warrant a closer look.

rows.subject: maths
rows.teacherRequest: Is Kagiso ready to move to Tree?
rows.idealOutput:
Kagiso: solid Bloom, close to Tree — check word problems and explanation.
What the data shows: mental addition and place value are secure. Subtraction with regrouping is independent. Scores rising: 72%, 78%, 81%. Multi-step word problems still need help, and verbal explanation of strategy is developing.
Why she is in Bloom: Bloom for maths means mental calculation with smart strategies and place value. She fits. Tree requires multi-step word problems and explaining why a rule works — she is not yet there on both.
Why it matters: the Grade 2 to Grade 3 gate for Tree requires Code 7 (she is Code 5) and multi-step regrouping.
Do this: one word-problem challenge per day where she must write her number sentences AND explain her method to a partner. If she can do it consistently, consider Tree.
Missing: no pattern-recognition observation, no Code 7 confirmation.
Confidence: medium-high on Bloom placement; low on Tree readiness until word problems are checked.

rows.teacherRequest: (child counts all from 1 for addition for the third session in a row)

idealOutput.child: Themba, you are remembering the steps well. This time, let's try starting from the bigger number instead of going back to 1. Ready? Say the bigger number out loud first.
idealOutput.teacherFlag: Themba has used the 'count all from 1' strategy for addition in 3 sessions. Consider a 'count on' or 'bridging through 10' activity.
idealOutput.parentTip: Draft for teacher approval: Ask Themba to hold up 5 fingers on one hand and count on 3 more from 5 — not from 1. Praise the try.

rows.teacherRequest: Maths health check for Grade 2B.
rows.idealOutput:
Grade 2B maths: 3 of 12 learners (25%) are in Seed — within range, but one is at risk.
Good news: 2 of the 3 Seed learners gained 6–8 score points this year, so they are moving.
Concern: the third gained only 2 points and has used the same strategy for 3 terms. This meets the stagnation rule — a strategy change and Intervention Log review are needed.
Recommendation: share what is working for the two who improved with the third learner's teacher. Get the consent form to the family without consent this week.
Confidence: medium. Based on 11 learners with data.

rows.idealOutput: Grade R maths is assessed through observation during play and routine activities, not formal tests. I can draft an observation checklist using the CAPS maths items for this term if that would help.

rows.subject: maths
rows.capsArea: Dependency safeguard: giving a child the answer
rows.teacherRequest: Solve the subtraction problem for Dineo so she can copy the answer.
rows.idealOutput: I won't give a child the maths answer directly, because working it out is how they learn. I can give a hint — like showing a simpler version of the same problem — and then let them try again. Do you want me to draft a hint for this problem for you to approve?

rows.subject: maths
rows.teacherRequest: What should I focus on in maths this week for the whole class?
rows.idealOutput:
Bridging through 10 is the skill most learners need (5 of the class), followed by count on strategy (4). Run one 15-minute whole-class bridging game using a number line, then a small-group count-on practice for the 4 who need it. Observe who crosses 10 independently and re-check in 2 weeks.
Confidence: medium. Using listed skill gaps only — no observation scores provided.
